records.headline: Local Author Hannah Fletcher publishes Husbands Career Mysteries
keywords: mysteries of the old north west
records.summary: Unsolved Cases get brought back to the Public Eye
article: Local author Hannah Fletcher, the wife of a distinguished Police Constable from Saskatchewan has published a book that reviews a lot of the cold unsolved cases from the last few decades across the North West Territories both before and after the formation of the modern provinces (Alberta, Saskatchewan) In the publication, she interviews many members of search parties sent out to investigate homicides and accidents, and witnesses.  It is both a great read and a great education in to the minds of some of the criminals unfortunately absconding within our lands.

One such example was from her own husband, who, during the summer of 1901 was part of the search party that went out to Black Pine's former Silver Mine in Saskatchewan, to try and find a missing nine year old boy.  During the interview, he mentioned his surprise to find that there were no less than four sets of footprints made at roughly the same time, two of which were adult.  Four, in a place that had laid undisturbed for at least a couple of decades, yet witness accounts all insisted that two boys went out alone exploring and found the cave leading to one of the shafts.  A mystery indeed!
Hannah Fletcher's New Book "Mysteries of the Old North West" is available in all good book stores across Canada.

records.headline: Local Author publishes book with interesting topic!
article: Local Author Henry "Harry" Whitmore, in fact the very same that forewent his inheritance of the famous Whitmore & Sons Iron and Machinery Company empire in favour of writing, has published a book.  Its an interesting publication, about objects or possessions that are found at the ends of the earth, sometimes literally, and certainly not where these objects belong!

I don't want to spoil the surprise but lets just say he details about Roman Coins in New York, Dinosaur fossils on top of inaccessible mountains, and even modern items in places thought undisturbed for decades.  Just take a look for yourself it is an interesting read indeed!
"Strange Things Found In Even Stranger Places" is now available in all good book stores and down at your local library.

records.headline: Remembering a great Guardian
records.summary: Lt. William McLeod dies peacefully aged 87
article: Lieutenant William McLeod, a veteran of the North West Mounted Police, died peacefully at the age of 87. Remembered for his steady leadership and long service on the frontier, McLeod was among the officers who took part in the 1901 search for missing boy Arnie Spencer. During that investigation, he recovered a gold pendant from the search area, an important piece of evidence in the case, and naturally the ownership remains classified as of the date of this article, due to the investigation officially still remaining open.

McLeod retired from the Force in 1920 and spent his later years in rural Ontario with his wife, Margaret, helping eith the Apple Orchard, and remaining active in his local community and a respected figure among former members of the Force.  Rest In Peace Lieutenant.

records.headline: Local Man Arrested in connection with Spencer disappearence
records.summary: Local Man Anthony Worthing arrested and later released in connection with disappearence of Arnie Spencer and death of Brother.
article: Local man Anthony Worthing (pictured second from left, bottom row) of Black Pine was arrested and questioned by police over the disappearence of Askew Arnold Spencer in July this year, and the death of his brother Andrew Spencer.  The technicalities of the interview have not been disclosed but we have confirmation that he made a statement willingly and was later released without charge.
